page: Amazon Web Services r8gb.16xlarge is an ARM-based, memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. The server features 64 physical cores across 64 dedicated vCPUs utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture clocked at 2.8 GHz with a 1:1 core-to-thread ratio. Cache hierarchy provides 64 KB L1 data cache per core, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory resources total 512.0 GB, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. Networking capabilities are configured with a 133 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The instance does not include bundled local storage or dedicated hardware GPUs, relying on external network-attached volumes for data persistence.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate high throughput across memory and multi-core operations. The instance achieved top-tier performance in uncached large-block memory bandwidth tests, registering 479.37 GB/s for reads and 236.27 GB/s for writes. Multi-core compute benchmarks reflect similar scaling, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 25669.0 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaching 671.45 GB/s. Software compilation with Clang scored 81539.0 in Geekbench. In-memory database metrics showed 132.72 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks alongside strong PassMark database scores. Conversely, single-threaded processing represents a trade-off, with Geekbench single-core scoring 1888.0 and single-core stress-ng tests sitting in the average bracket.

From an infrastructure cost-efficiency perspective, the r8gb.16xlarge leverages native ARM density to deliver high memory bandwidth and core counts without hyperthreading penalties. This configuration makes the instance suitable for large in-memory databases, Redis clusters, extensive Clang software compilation pipelines, and memory-intensive static web serving. Workloads with heavy single-thread dependencies or direct local disk requirements are less suited due to baseline per-core clock characteristics and the absence of attached local NVMe drives.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gb.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance delivering 64 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 physical cores at 2.8 GHz and 512.0 GB of system memory on the Nitro hypervisor platform. Featuring an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio and a 133 Gbps baseline network throughput, this server contains no local storage and no GPU accelerators. The hardware delivers top-tier memory bandwidth, reaching 479.37 GB/s read speeds, and demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded throughput in Clang software compilation and Redis operations totaling 132.72 million operations per second. While single-thread execution speeds are moderate, the dense physical core allocation and high memory bandwidth provide strong qualitative compute and memory density. It is specifically targeted for large-scale distributed caching, memory-resident database engines, parallel software builds, and high-throughput static web distribution.
